text: A field permits addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by every nonzero element. Rational numbers have this property. Zero remains excluded from division: multiplying zero by any candidate inverse still gives zero, never the required identity one.
title: Idea 1

text: Finite fields are possible too. Modulo the prime five, three has inverse two because their product six leaves remainder one. To solve three x equals four modulo five, multiply by two and reduce eight to three.
title: Idea 2

text: Check the result directly: three times three is nine, with remainder four. Modulo a prime, every nonzero remainder has an inverse. For composite moduli that statement can fail, so being a remainder system alone does not guarantee a field.
title: Idea 3

text: A field also determines which polynomial equations have solutions within it. The real numbers contain no square root of negative one. Extending to complex numbers adds i and its negative as roots, while keeping valid field arithmetic.
title: Idea 4
